sections.text: Introduction

This method 
is used for controlling Aluminum in outlet of filters ( in case of using Alum in 
clarification) and effluent of industrial waste water plant.

The maximum limit for Aluminum 
concentration in industrial wastewaters effluent according to Egyptian Law 
Number (4) for year 1994 is as follows:

For effluent of industrial wastewaters treatment, max. (3 mg/L) and tested once 
monthly.
For drinking water, max. (0.2 mg/L) and tested once weekly.

This experiment is tested for total
Aluminum ( soluble, colloidal and insoluble ).

Aluminum is the third most abundant element of the 
earths crust, occurring in minerals, rocks, and nearly all natural water 
as a soluble salt, a colloid or an insoluble compound or wastewater as a residual 
from alum coagulation. Recent work indicates that filtered water from a modern 
rapid sand filtration plant should have an aluminum concentration no greater 
than 50 μg/l.

The first draft was initiated by chemist: Esam 
Abdel Aziz Reviewed by chemist Mohamed A. Farag, revised by quality control 
chemist: Wael A. Tantawy at EDEPC, and accepted by eng: Fawzy Sobhy the Head Sector of 
Abu Sultan Power Station.
Significance

With Eriochrome cyanine R dye, 
dilute aluminum solutions buffered to a pH of 6.0 produce a red to pink complex 
that exhibits maximum absorption at 535 nm. The intensity of the developed 
color is influenced by the aluminum concentration, reaction time, temperature, 
pH, alkalinity and concentration of other ions in the sample. To compensate for 
color and turbidity, the aluminum in one portion of sample is complexed with 
EDTA to provide a blank.

The optimum 
aluminum range lies between 20 and 300 
mg/L but can be extended upward by sample dilution.

Sampling 
Handling

Collect samples in clean, acid-rinsed bottles. Preferably 
plastic, and examine them as soon as possible after collecting. If only soluble 
aluminum is to be determined. Filter a portion of sample through a 0.45 
μm membrane filter; discard first 50 ml of filtrate and use succeeding filtrate 
for the determination. Dont use filter paper, absorbent cotton, or glass wool 
for filtering any solution that is to be tested for aluminum, because they will 
remove most of the solution aluminum.
Interference

Negative errors are caused by both fluoride and polyphosphates, 
when the fluoride concentration is constant, the percentage error decreases with 
increasing amounts of aluminum. Because the fluoride concentration often is 
known or can be determined readily, fairly accurate results can be obtained by 
adding the known amount of fluoride to a set of standards.

A procedure is given for the 
removal of complex phosphate interference. Orthophosphate in concentration under 
10 mg/l doesn't interfere. The interference caused by even small amounts of 
alkalinity is removed by acidifying the sample just beyond the neutralization 
point of methyl orange. Sulfate doesn't interfere up to a concentration of 2000 
mg/l.

The interference of iron and manganese, two elements often found in water, is 
eliminated by adding ascorbic acid.
Safety Precautions

items:
Acids such as 
 sulfuric acid, nitric acid and others are 
 dangerous, so 
 you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep these acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do 
 not breathe them, use only in a hood.

sections.text: Reagents

Sulfuric Acid- H2SO4, 
0.02 N.

Ascorbic Acid Solution- 
Dissolve 0.1 g ascorbic acid in water and make up to 100 ml in a 
volumetric flask. Prepare fresh 
daily.

Buffer 
Reagent- Dissolve 136 
gm sodium acetate, NaC2H3O2 .3H2O 
in water, add 40 ml 1N acetic acid, and dilute
to 1L.

Stock Dye Solution, Use 
Solochrome Cyanine- Dissolve 
100 mg in water and dilute to 100
ml in a volumetric flask, 
this solution should have a pH of about 2.9.

Working 
Dye Solution- Dilute 10 ml of stock dye solution to 100 ml in a volumetric 
flask with water. Working solutions are stable for at least 6 months.

Stock Aluminum Solution- Dissolve 8.792 gm aluminum potassium sulfate Al K (SO4)2 .12H2O 
in water and dilute to1000 ml. ( 1 ml = 500 
mg 
Al ).

Standard Aluminum Solution- Dilute 10 ml stock aluminum 
solution to 1000 ml with water. ( 1 ml = 5 
mg 
Al ) prepare daily.

sections.text: Work to be Carried out
Preparation of Calibration Curve

Prepare a series of 
aluminum standard from 0 to 280 
mg/L 
based on a 25 ml sample.

Add 1 ml 0.02N H2SO4 
to each standard and mix. Add 1 ml ascorbic acid solution and mix. Add 10 ml buffer solution and 
mix with a volumetric pipet, add 5 ml working dye reagent 
and mix. Immediately make up to 50 ml with distilled water. Mix and let stand 
for 5 to 10 min.

Read absorbance on a 
spectrophotometer using wavelength of 535 nm.

Plot concentration of Al 
against absorbance.
